descriptions.zh:
我们发现这颗彗星实际上是一个巨大的巢穴，里面充斥着微小的昆虫。彗尾也不是冰雾，而是巢穴内部化学反应所排放的废气。

巢穴的外壳由死亡的昆虫组成，这使得内部生的物免受太空恶劣环境的影响。我们还发现了几种依附于巢穴生活的真菌。巢穴中存在一种复杂的共生关系，真菌依赖排放的废气维生，而昆虫则以真菌为食。
descriptions.en:
The comet was revealed to be a giant nest filled with tiny insects. The tail of the comet is not outgassed ice, but rather exhaust from chemical processes occurring deep inside the hive.

The outer layer of the nest is composed of dead individuals, protecting the living inside from the harsh conditions of space. We've also picked up several types of fungi living in and around the nest. There is a complex symbiosis at work here, with the fungi living off of the exhaust gasses and the insects feeding on the fungi.

descriptions.zh:
这是我们始料未及的发现：大脑集群。来自各种物种的湿糊糊的有机处理器官，成百上千个地连接在一起，悬浮在一个气球状的大型胶囊之中。它似乎已经被废弃，在近期的虚境风暴消散之后飘浮在深空之中。

胶囊之中有一个惊人的传感器阵列连接在大脑和胶囊之上，此外还有一个通信模块，能够呼叫舰船并发送信息，之前它对我们就是这么做的。

现在看来似乎是这些大脑自己联系了我们，解释了那一连串的信息。我们的[Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural]认为这个装置的初衷是测试有机体对虚境风暴的反应。考虑到这些悬浮大脑内不稳定的残留灵能，尝试与其连接可能会带来危险。
descriptions.en:
We could never have anticipated our discovery: brains. Organic, squishy central processing organs from all sorts of species. Hundreds and hundreds of them, all linked together and suspended inside a large balloon-like capsule. It appears to be derelict, left floating in the depths of space after a recent Shroud Storm dissipated.

The capsule contains an incredible array of sensors attached to the brains and the balloon, and there is also a communication module, capable of hailing ships and transmitting information, just as it did to us.

It seems likely that the brains themselves contacted us, explaining the cacophony of messages. Our [Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural] think the construction was designed to measure organic responses to a Shroud Storm. Given the unstable psionic residue within these floating minds, attempting to interface them would only lead to disaster.

descriptions.zh:
[Root.Owner.GetScientistPluralCapital]报告称这个空间站的大部分是由常见的固定材料建成的，这些物质勉强维持着空间站不至于散架。随着我们深入这座结构，构成空间站的物质从金属合金过渡成了塑料等其他材料。

在空间站的核心处，我们发现了一台机器正在高效运转，它不断地拆解有机原料并将其转化为我们之前见到的东西。

在运行DNA模拟模型后，我们的[Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural]只能得出结论，这些原料可能是空间站的前住民。
descriptions.en:
[Root.Owner.GetScientistPluralCapital] report that much of this space station is constructed from everyday stationary objects, barely holding it together. Deeper into the structure, the materials transition from metal alloys to plastics and other substances.

Inside the heart of the construct we found a machine, still in the process of efficiently deconstructing organic material and shaping it into the very items encountered so far.

After running a DNA simulation model, our [Root.Owner.GetScientistPlural] have been forced to conclude that the material likely came from the former inhabitants of this outpost.

label.zh: 看看我们能发现些什么。
label.en: See if we can't gain something here.

descriptions.zh:
[root.leader.GetName]汇报了自[from.GetAffectedStormType]过境以来，[From.GetStarName]的聚变反应所发生的奇妙变化。

显然，这个风暴引发了恒星内核某种意想不到的核反应，导致其对流区稳定地释放出[from.GetEarnedResources]。

这些复杂而特殊的反应产生了我们所观察到的这些不寻常的多色闪光。无论如何，在一段时间内这的都会一直是一个值得仔细研究的来源。
descriptions.en:
[root.leader.GetName] reports fascinating changes in [From.GetStarName]'s fusion reactions since the passage of the [from.GetAffectedStormType].

It appears that the storm induced unexpected nuclear reactions within the star's core, resulting in a steady release of [from.GetEarnedResources] from its convective zones.

These complex and idiosyncratic reactions are producing the unusual polychromatic flaring we have observed. In any case, it will continue to be a source worthy of close study for some time.

descriptions.zh:
[root.leader.GetName]发现，沉积于[from.solar_system.GetName]星系的小行星具有高度不稳定的磁性质，导致它们在恒星系中现有的磁层上发生随机的弹跳。

[root.leader.GetName]通过给每个小行星施加磁场补偿器进行了稳定，使其轨道规范化并使其便于进行资源开采。
descriptions.en:
[root.leader.GetName] discovered that the asteroids deposited in the [from.solar_system.GetName] system possess highly unstable magnetic fields, causing them to ricochet haphazardly off the system's existing magnetospheres.

[root.leader.GetName] stabilized them by adding magnetic compensators to each asteroid, regulating their trajectories and thus making them amenable to resource extraction efforts.

descriptions.zh:
我们已经确定了§H[from.solar_system.GetName]§!星系中遇险信号的来源，那一艘严重受损但仍在运作的商船。

乘员声称他们被§H[from.GetAffectedStormType]§!撞离了航线很远。风暴也烧毁了他们的引擎，让飞船和里面的东西滞留在我们的空间里。

如果我们能帮忙的话，他们愿意交出一部分货物。
descriptions.en:
We have identified the source of the distress signal in the §H[from.solar_system.GetName]§! system as a heavily damaged but still functioning mercantile vessel.

The occupants claim they have been knocked a great distance off course by the §H[from.GetAffectedStormType]§!. The storm has also burnt out their engines, leaving the ship and its contents stranded in our space.

They are willing to part with a portion of their cargo if we can help.

label.zh: 夺走他们的生命以及货物。

descriptions.zh:
§H[from.solar_system.GetName]§!星系内的异常读数源自一片由§H[from.GetAffectedStormType]§!的余波所残留下的不寻常的碎片阵列。

这个漂浮的实体是由一团无定形的宇宙污泥在风暴的极端压力下锻造而成。它的无数组成元素形成了一种独特的活性化合物。

对其化学成分的深度研究可以对产生它的条件提供有价值的星际气象学洞见。
descriptions.en:
The erratic sensor readings in the §H[from.solar_system.GetName]§! system are derived from an exceptional debris formation left in the wake of the §H[from.GetAffectedStormType]§!.

This drifting entity is an amorphous blob of cosmic sludge, forged in the extreme pressures of the storm. Its innumerable constituent elements have formed a uniquely reactive compound.

Focused study of its chemistry could yield valuable astrometeorological insights into the conditions that produced it.

descriptions.zh:
§H[from.solar_system.GetName]§!星系中的物体是一颗古老人造卫星的残骸，上面装有复杂的星际气象探测阵列。我们认为它是伴随着§H[from.GetAffectedStormType]§!横跨星系漂星过海而来的。

它已严重损坏无法维修，但中央数据库包含了大量的信息贮藏可以为我们所用。

卫星的其余部分就只能作为废品进行打捞了。
descriptions.en:
The object in the §H[from.solar_system.GetName]§! system is the wreckage of an ancient satellite equipped with complex astrometeorological sensor arrays. We believe that it was swept a great distance across the galaxy in the wake of the §H[from.GetAffectedStormType]§!.

Now damaged beyond repair, its central databases contain a vast store of information that we can repurpose for our own needs.

The rest of the satellite is only salvageable as scrap.

descriptions.zh: 我们发现，§H[from.solar_system.GetName]§!星系的怪异物体其实是一大团来自某种太空生物的有机残留物。由于所有可供识别的特征都被宇宙风暴撕碎了，所以无法对这些生物碎片进行准确分类。
descriptions.en: The foreign object in the §H[from.solar_system.GetName]§! system was discovered to be a large mass of organic remains originating from some type of spaceborne fauna. Having had any identifiable features shredded apart by the cosmic storm, it is impossible to correctly catalog the biological debris.

descriptions.zh: 幸运的是，大部分仍可食用。
descriptions.en: Fortunately, it remains mostly edible.

descriptions.zh: [leader.GetName]确信，对该生物遗骸进行更详细的法医分析将揭示更多有关其起源性质的信息，以及§Y[from.GetAffectedStormType]§!对类似太空生物的影响。
descriptions.en: [leader.GetName] is confident that a more detailed forensic analysis of the creature's remains would reveal more information about the nature of its origins and the effects of a §Y[from.GetAffectedStormType]§! on similar space faring organisms.

descriptions.zh:
经过了谨慎的解剖，这团肉块究竟属于什么物种仍是个谜。在风暴中心遭受的巨大破坏使它失去了一切可供识别的特征和遗传标记。

然而，在这项研究的过程中，我们获得了对§Y宇宙风暴§!组成的洞见，了解了其对外星生物质的破坏性影响。
descriptions.en:
After careful dissection, the original species of this visceral mass remains a mystery. The extraordinary damage taken in the epicenter of the storm has stripped it of any recognizable features or genetic markers.

However, in the process of this study we have gained insight into the composition of §YCosmic Storms§! and their devastating effects on xenobiological matter.

options.script: name = FASCINATING

descriptions.zh:
§H[solar_system.GetName]§!星系内的三只缇扬奇信号经过识别后发现是一伙流离失所、营养不良的幼崽。

§Y宇宙风暴§!将这些幼崽与它们的大群分开，迫使他们自力更生。

它们看来不太可能在幽深的太空中存活太久。我们的传感器显示它们整在试图呼叫鲸群，但没有成功。
descriptions.en:
The three Tiyanki signatures in the §H[solar_system.GetName]§! system have been identified as a set of displaced and malnourished calves.

The §YCosmic Storm§! has separated these calves from their larger pod, leaving them to fend for themselves.

They are unlikely to survive for long in open space. Our sensors show they are attempting to call for their pod but are having no success.

descriptions.zh: 我们的通讯系统可以用来增强它们的呼救声，吸引它们的群体进入恒星系。
descriptions.en: Our communication systems could be used to boost their cries for help and attract their pod into the system.

descriptions.zh: 我们可以放大它们呼救的声音，把它们当作诱饵，引来一顿更大的大餐。
descriptions.en: We could boost their cries for help and use them as bait to draw in a larger feast.

tooltips.zh: 向你的['concept_vivarium']中增加3只随机稀有度的§Y缇扬奇幼体§!
tooltips.en: Add 3 §YTiyanki Hatchling§! of random rarity to your ['concept_vivarium']

descriptions.zh:
缇扬奇的成兽在听到了三只幼崽被放大的叫声后，再度现身在§H[solar_system.GetName]§!星系中。

年轻的缇扬奇重新回到了鲸群，现在已经恢复了快乐和健康。

母鲸在我们的科研船附近留下了一大堆物质碎片，似乎是在感谢我们的帮助。令我们惊讶的是，这件奇怪的礼物中包含了好几种可用的材料。
descriptions.en:
A Tiyanki cow and bull have both appeared in the §H[solar_system.GetName]§! system having heard the amplified cries of the three displaced calves.

The juvenile Tiyanki have been reintegrated back into their pod, and already appear much happier and healthier.

The cow has deposited a large mass of debris near our science vessel, seemingly as some kind of appreciation for our assistance. To our surprise this curious offering contains several usable materials.

descriptions.zh: 当然，这些大东西才是真正的猎物；我们已经准备好猎杀了。
descriptions.en: Of course, these larger beasts are the true prize; primed and ready for the slaughter.
